Your virtual assistant onboarding process, step by step

Start the virtual assistant onboarding process with one recurring task. In your virtual assistant onboarding checklist, record what the task needs, who owns it, which tools are involved and what a finished result looks like.

  1. 01

    Discovery

    List the recurring work, current tools, priorities and coverage needs. Identify who can approve scope and access.

  2. 02

    Scope and matching

    Define outputs, capacity, responsibilities and approval limits. Confirm the skills and working arrangement needed.

  3. 03

    Onboarding

    Document a starting workflow, give only the access it requires and run a small example through review.

  4. 04

    Ongoing delivery

    Assign work through the agreed channel, record completed items and surface exceptions with a named next owner.

  5. 05

    Review and continuity

    Review work against the original scope, agree adjustments and document how handovers or absences would be managed.

Start with a daily brief.

Use a daily brief to learn how to work with a virtual assistant. Your virtual assistant onboarding checklist should name the reviewer and the decisions they receive.

Make each decision easy to route.

Your virtual assistant onboarding process needs a responsible person on both sides. Learning how to work with a virtual assistant includes agreeing how exceptions are routed.

You provide

Priorities, authorised access, source information and a named person for approvals.

Delivery owner

Written task instructions, an agreed work log, questions and exceptions that need a decision.

Review together

Check completed work, update the instructions and decide how to handle changes or absences.

Plan access and approvals

Know what to review and when.

A virtual assistant onboarding checklist should include the reporting window. Your virtual assistant onboarding process can then account for routine work and urgent requests separately.

CadenceWork in scopeWhat you review

Decide whether to expand the scope.

Test your virtual assistant onboarding process. Record the result in your virtual assistant onboarding checklist.

  • Compare the result with the example you provided. Note any changes needed to tone, format or accuracy.
  • Check whether routine work could proceed and whether exceptions reached the right person.
  • Update the instructions, coverage and permissions before adding another queue or system.

Build your virtual assistant onboarding checklist

A virtual assistant onboarding checklist turns discovery into specific decisions. Use the conversation to establish how to work with a virtual assistant in your existing systems.

Bring examples to your virtual assistant onboarding process

Choose a routine request that already has a finished example. Explain where it arrived, what a good outcome looked like and whether the person handling it had to ask for a decision.

Name the constraints

Discuss coverage, deadlines and the systems that are allowed. Explain when the client should be contacted directly and which types of requests require a specialist or approver.

Agree the first milestone

Choose the first output and the person who will review it. Put the review date and instructions somewhere both sides can find them. Decide what needs to happen before work moves from a trial to normal delivery.

Run a small batch through the whole process.

Test your virtual assistant onboarding process on normal and unusual requests. Update the virtual assistant onboarding checklist when a rule or approval route is missing.

Add tools to your virtual assistant onboarding checklist

Put the input in the same place the assistant will normally find it. Run the first task with the permissions it actually needs and confirm that the output reaches the right workspace.

Review the record as well as the result

Check whether the item can be traced from request to result. Confirm which version was reviewed and that the next owner or approver can see the information they need.

Review your virtual assistant onboarding process

Write down the change and show an example. If a draft reply missed a useful deadline, explain which source to check and where the deadline should be recorded next time.

Handle changes without losing the work.

A virtual assistant onboarding checklist should cover changes in tools, people or timing. Your virtual assistant onboarding process needs a review before those changes take effect.

When volume changes

Review what arrived, which deadlines are affected and whether a temporary queue makes sense. Get approval before extending a commitment beyond the coverage already agreed.

When the owner changes

Provide the new owner with the working instructions, the latest output and a list of decisions still open. Confirm their access to the records before the previous owner steps away.

When the scope changes

Describe the new task separately from the existing work. Agree the tools, permissions, coverage and first example to review. If the change needs more capacity, see when to revisit the quote.

Decide what to improve before adding volume.

Use the first month to refine how to work with a virtual assistant. Your virtual assistant onboarding checklist should reflect the instructions that proved useful.

Keep what works

Record the examples that met the standard so they can be reused during training or a change in coverage.

Correct the rules that cause rework

Clarify any instruction that produced the same mistake twice. Update the source guidance and agree how to check it on the next batch.

Review the next request

Use a fresh example to see whether the change solved the problem. Keep the original approval boundary unless a responsible person agrees to change it.

Follow a request from the queue to the finished record.

Follow one request through the virtual assistant onboarding process. Your virtual assistant onboarding checklist should connect the source, review decision and finished record.

At intake

The assistant links the request to the calendar entry and checks the time zone, attendees and deadline. They mark whether the request includes new timing options or needs a reply before any slot can be offered.

While the work is open

The assistant drafts options and checks them against approved scheduling rules. If moving the meeting affects another commitment, the executive receives the choice and its impact together so they can respond without opening multiple threads.

When the task is complete

The assistant updates the approved invite, confirms the agenda link and records what was sent and when. The meeting owner can see the new time and the one item still awaiting an answer.

Agree what moves to the front of the queue.

A virtual assistant onboarding process needs a rule for urgent work. Discuss how to work with a virtual assistant when several requests arrive at the same time.

Time-sensitive work

Identify tasks that affect a commitment already made, such as a promised customer update or a meeting starting soon. State when to notify the owner and where they will see the message.

Routine work

Assign a regular review window for items that can wait until the next pass. Give the assistant a way to distinguish the ones they can complete independently from the ones that need approval.

Missing information

Leave blocked items visible with the question that needs answering and who can answer it. Set a follow-up time so a request that cannot move today still appears in the next review.

Add another queue when the first one is stable.

Reuse the virtual assistant onboarding checklist for a new queue. Your virtual assistant onboarding process should still check its different permissions, reviewers and deadlines.

Compare the starting rules

Look at how requests enter the new queue, what a finished result looks like and who owns exceptions. Reuse instructions only when the same people and approval boundaries apply.

Test a small batch

Pick an ordinary case and an exception. Have the new reviewer compare the outputs with the agreed examples and confirm where questions should go before the assistant handles a larger volume.

Agree what to check next

Track whether the original queue still gets attention when the new one is busy. Review the two queues separately so the team can tell whether a delay came from added volume, an unclear rule or unavailable reviewers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask how to work with a virtual assistant using a specific task. A virtual assistant onboarding checklist can help organise the answers before work starts.

Will I work with a dedicated assistant?

Confirm the assignment model, named point of contact and any specialist involvement in the scope before work begins.

How do we agree coverage and working hours?

Share your time zone, required overlap and the tasks that are time sensitive. The scope should record the agreed coverage and how exceptions are handled.

How is access handled?

Discuss the accounts, data and permissions needed for each task. Start with the minimum access needed and agree how it will be removed at handover.

What should I prepare before onboarding starts?

Your virtual assistant onboarding checklist should include a normal request, an exception, the expected output and the responsible reviewer. Add the systems involved and which permissions your account owner has approved for the first task.

How do we review the first result?

Use the first pass to check how to work with a virtual assistant in practice. Compare the result with your example and give specific feedback on accuracy, missing context, format and the decisions that still need your input.

Does the virtual assistant onboarding process cover additional workflows?

A new queue should have its own inputs, review owner and approval rules. Test a small batch and confirm that the original work still receives the agreed attention before expanding the ongoing scope.

Make room for the work only you can do.

Tell us which task you’d like to hand off and what a good result looks like. Start with one piece of work that comes up regularly.
